01.reason: An orphan lease whose wine soured, then only a legal comparison between Rav Kahana and Rav Ashi; one incident followed by discussion, nothing changes.

02.reason: Rabbi and R. Hiyya walk, veer aside, see R. Yehuda ben Kenosa striding ahead, reach him and Rabbi confronts him: several actions, conflict and a resolution.

03.reason: A setting (Rav Aha enters a meal) framing a halakhic exchange about who blesses; like Shabbat 147a, the setting plus question and answer is not a story.

04.reason: Rav Huna sees a man drink water before havdala and rebukes him: one real event, then mainly speech, cited as a halakhic position.

05.reason: People come before Rav Yitzhak bar Ami and he rules on path width; coming before a rabbi and the ruling are the only events.

06.reason: Rav Yitzhak bar Yosef buys a utensil and is told immersion is not required; one event then a ruling, no stated outcome.

07.reason: A dialogue between a heretic and R. Hanina about Balaam's age, with no event and no real conflict; speech only.

08.reason: A man testifies before R. Hanina that someone is a firstborn; a case brought to a rabbi with question and answer, nothing narrated changes.

09.reason: A man resolves to go up to Eretz Yisrael to hear a ruling from its source, travels, and learns it was misreported: a real journey, but mostly a halakhic Q&A.

10.reason: Four sages need a head, set a contest, all but Abaye are refuted, Rabba sees it and calls on Abaye to begin: actions and a change in status.

11.reason: A halakhic debate between R. Yohanan and Reish Lakish ending in silence and a quip; ordinary scholarly back-and-forth, not conflict in the R-C2 sense.

12.reason: R. Elazar b. R. Yosei's one-line testimony that he saw the curtain in Rome, cited as evidence for a halakha; nothing follows.

13.reason: A one-line eyewitness wonder by Rabba bar bar Hana (the I-myself-saw shape left open under R-C5); an observation with little event or change.

14.reason: Reports of how Rabba, R. Yohanan and R. Asi habitually trimmed kidney fat, then legal discussion; practice cited as evidence.

15.reason: A halakhic question and answer between Rav Aha and Rav Ashi; no event.

16.reason: Legal objection citing a ruling of Rava and a sent ruling of Rav Huna bar Avin; precedents alluded to as evidence, no narrative.

17.reason: R. Yohanan's saying about his tenth son's bone is cited only to attribute an interpretation; no event is narrated.

18.reason: Levi checking his collection of baraitot and the ensuing legal argument; a source citation, not a story.

19.reason: R. Yannai sees a man give charity publicly and rebukes him for shaming the poor man: one real event, then speech with conflict, cited as an exemplum.

20.reason: An incident of someone swallowing a leech and R. Nehemya permitting heating water on Shabbat: one event followed by a ruling, nothing further narrated.
